description: Biz, bilime, teknolojiye, uzaya ve keşfetmeye tutkuyla bağlı bir ekibiz. Cosmic Heroes olarak amacımız yalnızca bir yarışmaya katılmak değil, bilimin ve teknolojinin gücünü kullanarak gerçek dünyadaki problemlere yenilikçi ve uygulanabilir çözümler üretmek. 2025 deneyimimizle uzay teknolojileri, bilimsel araştırma ve takım çalışması alanlarında önemli tecrübeler kazandık. Bu yıl çok daha iddialı hedeflerle, somut verilerden ve bilimsel temellerden yararlanarak yeni bir projeyle karşınızdayız.
summary: The Smart Plant Cultivation and Water Management System for Space is an intelligent system we developed to support the growth of plants in a microgravity environment without the use of soil. In our project, plant roots are placed within cotton, and the moisture level in the root zone is monitored via a sensor. When the moisture level falls below a predefined threshold, the DENEYAP Kart microcontroller triggers the system, displaying a "water required" alert on an LCD screen and activating a water pump to initiate automatic irrigation. During irrigation, an MH-RD water detection module monitors for the presence of water; once the specified condition is met, the DENEYAP Kart stops the pump, thereby ending the irrigation process. Our project aims to simplify plant care during space missions, ensure the controlled use of water, and reduce the workload of astronauts. It serves as an adaptable prototype that could contribute to plant cultivation efforts in future missions to the Moon and Mars. AI
details:
Our project, Smart Plant Growing and Smart Water Management System in Space, has been developed to support soil-free plant cultivation in microgravity environments and to automatically manage plants' water needs.

Working Principle:

In our project, the plant's roots will be placed inside cotton. Instead of using traditional soil, cotton will serve as the initial growing medium for the plant. The moisture level inside the cotton surrounding the roots will be monitored by a moisture sensor.

When the moisture level falls below a predefined threshold, the DENEYAP Board microcontroller will detect this condition and display a water-need warning on the LCD screen. It will then activate the water pump to start automatic irrigation. During irrigation, the MH-RD water detection module will detect contact with water. When the predefined detection condition is met, the DENEYAP Board will stop the motor and display a message on the LCD screen indicating that the irrigation process is complete.

Technologies and Hardware Used:

  • DENEYAP Board: The microcontroller that controls the system.
  • Moisture Sensor: Monitors the moisture level inside the cotton.
  • MH-RD Water Detection Module: Detects water contact during irrigation.
  • Water Pump: Transfers water to the plant's root area.
  • LCD Display: Shows moisture warnings and the system's operating status.
  • Cotton: Serves as the initial growing medium instead of soil.
  • Programming: A programmed control system is used to process sensor data, control the motor, and display information on the LCD screen.

Project Benefits and Intended Impact:

Our project aims to make plant cultivation easier on space stations and during future Moon and Mars missions. Through automatic water management, we aim to reduce the time astronauts spend caring for plants, ensure controlled water usage, and help maintain the moisture level required by plants.

Creativity and Innovation:

The innovative aspect of our project is the combination of soil-free plant cultivation with a sensor-based automatic irrigation system. Our system monitors the plant's moisture needs, starts irrigation when water is needed, and stops irrigation when the predefined water-detection condition is met. In this way, it aims to automate plant care and reduce the need for human intervention.

Factors Considered by Our Team:

While designing our project, we considered the challenges associated with using soil in space environments, the limited availability of water, the moisture requirements of plant roots, the importance of automatic control, and the workload of astronauts. We also aimed to make the system simple, adaptable, and suitable for further development for different space missions.

Our project is a prototype inspired by NASA's research on plant cultivation and water management in space. It combines soil-free growing methods with smart automation. Further development, particularly in controlled water delivery to plant roots and nutrient-solution management, will be necessary before the current design can be adapted for use in microgravity environments.
